meta.author: Agent 2 - World, Systems and Gameplay Simulation
meta.status: PROVISIONAL - engineering assumptions, NOT canon, NOT measured
meta.purpose: Map the register's authored scene categories to simulation tiers so the population cost of the world is arithmetic over authored data rather than an engineering guess.
meta.separation_rule: Register data lives in the Drive registers and Tools/canon fixtures. This file holds ONLY engineering assumptions. No number in this file may be presented as coming from the register. Every entry states its rationale and confidence.

tier_definitions.NAMED: Tier 1. Full ACharacter with StateTree, full animation, dialogue, quest hooks. Reserved for the 13 approved supporting-cast names (OAD-15) plus Adanna. Never used for population filler.
tier_definitions.CROWD: Tier 2. Mass entity with LOD-ticked StateTree processor. Reacts to player, can be greeted. No dialogue tree, no quests.
tier_definitions.SCRIPTED: Lightweight scripted activity. One performer animating on a fixed loop at a marked spot. No AI, no perception, no navigation, no state beyond the loop. This is the tier the Technical Director specifically required: an ambient activity does NOT need an individually simulated NPC with an AI controller.
tier_definitions.BACKGROUND: Tier 3. Instanced, vertex-animated, no logic tick at all. Silhouette and motion only from a distance.
tier_definitions.NONE: Nothing simulated. Geometry and dressing only. Used where the register says 'Gameplay relevance: None required' AND there is no depicted person.

AMBIENT NPC SCENE.rationale: The register names people and interaction ('greet her') in these scenes, so they need reaction, but they are background life, not story actors. 20 such scenes game-wide, 14 in Chapter 1.
AMBIENT NPC SCENE.register_basis: Category definition + 'What the player can interact with' lines, e.g. CH01-SCN-001 'Greet her; she answers without stopping.'

WORLD ACTIVITY SCENE.rationale: These depict one person performing one craft or task at a fixed station (blacksmith, loom, pots, kitchen, harvest). The register gives no interaction and no routine variation within the scene. A looping scripted performer reproduces the authored intent at a fraction of crowd cost.
WORLD ACTIVITY SCENE.register_basis: e.g. CH01-SCN-010 'The Blacksmith at Work' - FULLY ENTERABLE, no interaction required, no routine beyond the task.

ATMOSPHERIC SCENE.rationale: The register usually asks for the space itself ('Goats at Dusk' has one boy driving goats; 'The Well at Noon' has no NPC). One scripted performer at most. Where the register states an NPC, the register count wins over this default.
ATMOSPHERIC SCENE.register_basis: CH01-SCN-025 lists 'One boy'; CH01-SCN-032 The Well at Noon lists no NPC. Verified divergence within one category, hence the lower confidence.
ATMOSPHERIC SCENE.caution: Do not assume zero. The register explicitly populates some atmospheric scenes.

ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING.rationale: These scenes are explicitly about the object and what is absent. CH01-SCN-024 'NPCs present. None.' Adding a simulated person would contradict the authored intent.
ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING.register_basis: CH01-SCN-024 'The House No One Lives In' - 'NPCs present. None.'; 'Gameplay relevance. None required. Rewards attention only.'

ENTERABLE INTERIOR.rationale: Interiors are entered briefly and depict a household activity (kitchen shelter, sleeping corner, compound store). One scripted occupant unless the register says otherwise.
ENTERABLE INTERIOR.register_basis: CH01-SCN-007 Sleeping Corner, CH01-SCN-005 The Kitchen Shelter - reachable interiors with implied household presence.

EXTERIOR MICRO-LOCATION.rationale: Traversal spaces: a gap between houses, a path behind houses, a doorway without a house. The register gives them no NPCs and no interaction. They exist to be walked through.
EXTERIOR MICRO-LOCATION.register_basis: Category definition; CH01-SCN-021, 022, 023, 034 all have no NPC lines.

EXPLORATION SCENE.rationale: Exploration rewards attention to place, not people. No NPCs in the register for these.
EXPLORATION SCENE.register_basis: CH01-SCN-040 The Light Gap, CH01-SCN-043 A Path That Gives Up.

SECONDARY STORY SCENE.rationale: Story scenes are authored beats with specific content. They get full-fidelity treatment. In Chapter 1 the single secondary story scene is Memory 1, which depicts no living NPC in its discovery location.
SECONDARY STORY SCENE.register_basis: CH01-SCN-046 'NPCs present. None.' - the memory is delivered through place, object, sound and interaction, not a person (OAD-32).

MAIN STORY SCENE.rationale: Four exist game-wide, all in Chapter 8. Full fidelity by definition.
MAIN STORY SCENE.register_basis: Register count table: 4 main story scenes, all Chapter 8.

INCIDENTAL SCENE.rationale: Two exist game-wide, both Chapter 8. Treated as a single scripted beat until their detail blocks are read.
INCIDENTAL SCENE.register_basis: Register count table only; no detail blocks read yet.

unmapped_category_fallback.rationale: SAFE DEFAULT. If a new scene category appears in a future register version, it must not be silently treated as free. Scripted is the cheapest tier that still depicts a person; the validator reports every fallback use so the category can be mapped deliberately.

crowd_concurrency_ratio._note: The register's NPC count is how many people a scene DEPICTS, not how many must be simulated simultaneously. Ratio converts depicted to concurrent.

cost_units._note: Relative cost units for budget arithmetic only. NOT milliseconds, NOT a frame-time claim. Calibrated against the chapter ceiling below so that Chapter 1's authored content fits the stated frame budget. Must be replaced by measured cost once a capture exists.

access_multipliers._note: Independent cost multiplier applied after tier cost. Derived from the access level's streaming/collision/tick policy in Docs/WORLD_ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.

chapter_limits._note: Chapter ceilings. A derived budget exceeding these fails validation. Set so that Chapter 1, which has 14 ambient NPC scenes and 8 world activity scenes, fits.

open_questions_for_directorate.question: Are 'World Activity Scene' depictions intended to be observable in detail up close (the player can stand in the smithy), or can they be screen-space-distant loops?
open_questions_for_directorate.impact: Determines whether SCRIPTED tier needs full-rate animation when the player is within 3 m.

open_questions_for_directorate.question: Does every 'Ambient NPC Scene' need to react to Adanna, or may some be unaware of her by design?
open_questions_for_directorate.impact: Reaction requires CROWD tier perception; unaware scenes could drop to SCRIPTED and halve their cost.

open_questions_for_directorate.question: Are depicted child NPCs to be animated at the same fidelity as adults?
open_questions_for_directorate.impact: Child-specific animation sets and the non-combat targeting rule both constrain the crowd processor.
